Hi Casey — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Marcus (infra/sizing) and Tessa (AM) so you get both the operational and commercial view.

Quick summary of what we recommend for an 8→16 renewal:
- Commercial: amend the monthly commit from 8 GPUs to 16 GPUs on the renewal effective date. We price the incremental commit at a committed-discounted rate; the uplift is ~18% on list for this increase (we can confirm exact unit rates once procurement gives PO cadence).
- Activation model: staged activation (recommended):
  * Week 0 (agreement signed): reserve 16-slot pool in our scheduling plane; billing transitions pro-rata from the effective date.
  * Weeks 1–2: ramp to 12 GPUs—validation with your perf test suite and KV cache warmup.
  * Weeks 3–6: full activation to 16 GPUs and throughput tuning.
- SLA / throughput: we will provide a throughput target per-allocated GPU based on the target model family you run. For your <acme-gen> workload we estimate sustained 420–480 tokens/sec per GPU at 512-token sequence length. If we can lock a quick perf run we’ll produce a verified throughput table for the order form.
- Fallbacks: automated routing to a compatible quantized variant if the pool is transiently unavailable; we can set policy to preserve latency SLOs with slightly reduced quality if you prefer.

I attached a short mutual-action plan (Acme_Renewal_MA_Plan.xlsx) that outlines dates, owners, and deliverables. Can you confirm: procurement contact and the PO workflow?

Happy to book a 30-minute call Monday or Tuesday next week — propose Tue 9/16 10am PT.

Best,

Casey / Soojin — quick operational notes from our side so procurement has the technical constraints:

1) Pool reservation and placement
   - We will reserve a 16-GPU reserved pool in the same region (us-west-2) to avoid cross-region egress. The pool will be isolated for your tenancy with dedicated routing.

2) Phased cutover details
   - During Weeks 1–2 (ramp to 12 GPUs) we’ll do daily perf checks and KV cache warmups; your engineers should run their baseline prompts against the staging endpoint.
   - Week 3 toggle to production traffic split (gradual traffic % shift); Week 4–6 full traffic and golden-checks.

3) Throughput and model variants
   - We recommend pinning to the verified variant for production and enabling an automatic fallback variant that’s quantized (reduced memory footprint) for transient capacity pressure.

4) Migration windows and maintenance
   - We need 2x 2-hour maintenance windows (off-peak) scheduled during the ramp for kernel tuning and kernel selection validation.

I’ve attached our internal playbook we’ll use to coordinate the cutover (staged-activation-playbook.pdf). Happy to walk through it on the kickoff call.

—Marcus
